# The question, in one sentence

## 

> **Do the three contraceptive methods differ in vaginal microbiome community composition or in the prevalence of bacterial vaginosis?**

# What we did

## 

- **Dataset:** Study B contraception trial — 93 participants in three arms:
  injectable (39), pill (28), and ring (26).
- **Count table:** 220 species in rows, 93 samples in columns.
- **Pre-filter:** Dropped the 86 species never observed in any sample, leaving
  134 species. This removes noise and follows the QC recommendation.
- **QC flags carried forward:** one shallow sample (B006, 5,247 reads); two
  samples missing cytokines. None were dropped from the primary analysis.
- **Community composition:** Bray–Curtis distance on compositional shares +
  PERMANOVA; Aitchison distance as a robustness check; `betadisper` to check
  equal dispersion.
- **BV prevalence:** Fisher's exact test on the clinical Nugent label
  (negative / intermediate / positive); molecular community type
  (*Lactobacillus* fraction ≥ 0.5) as a second opinion.

# Figure 1 — Community composition by arm

## 

![PCoA of Bray–Curtis distances, coloured by contraceptive arm](02-community-composition_files/figure-html/ord-arm-1.png){width="70%"}

**Figure 1.** Principal coordinate analysis of Bray–Curtis distances between
samples. Each point is one participant. The three colours (injectable, pill,
ring) are intermixed across the plot — no arm occupies its own region. Axis 1
explains 33.8% of the variation, axis 2 explains 26.0%.

# Figure 2 — What actually structures the composition

## 

![Same PCoA, coloured by BV status](02-community-composition_files/figure-html/what-structures-1.png){width="70%"}

**Figure 2.** The same Bray–Curtis ordination, now coloured by bacterial
vaginosis status. BV status explains 24% of the compositional variation
(p = 0.001), while contraceptive arm explains only about 3% (p = 0.15). The
community varies with BV, not with contraceptive method.

# Figure 3 — BV prevalence by arm

## 

![BV prevalence with 95% confidence intervals](03-bv-by-arm_files/figure-html/prevalence-plot-1.png){width="70%"}

**Figure 3.** BV prevalence by contraceptive arm, with 95% confidence
intervals. Injectable: 19/39 (48.7%); pill: 10/28 (35.7%); ring: 10/26
(38.5%). The intervals overlap heavily, consistent with no true difference
(Fisher exact p = 0.45).

# Choice we made — community composition

## 

| | |
|---|---|
| **Route A (kept as primary)** | Bray–Curtis distance on compositional shares |
| **Route B (kept as check)** | Aitchison distance (CLR + Euclidean) |
| **Why keep both?** | Bray–Curtis is the ecology standard; Aitchison is the compositional-data standard. Agreement means the "no difference" verdict is not a distance artefact. |
| **Source I opened** | Anderson 2001, *A new method for non-parametric multivariate analysis of variance*; Aitchison 1986, *The Statistical Analysis of Compositional Data*. |

**Result:** both distances agree — R² ≈ 0.03, p ≈ 0.15.

# Choice we made — BV definition

## 

| | |
|---|---|
| **Route A (kept as primary)** | Clinical BV label from Nugent score |
| **Route B (kept as check)** | Molecular community type: *Lactobacillus* fraction ≥ 0.5 vs. anaerobe |
| **Why keep both?** | Nugent is the clinical reference; the molecular type is a sequencing-based second opinion. Agreement means the result is not sensitive to how BV is defined. |
| **Source I opened** | Nugent et al. 1991, *Journal of Clinical Microbiology*; Ravel et al. 2011, *PNAS* on vaginal community state types. |

**Result:** both definitions agree — clinical p = 0.45, molecular p = 0.53.

# The answer, stated plainly

## 

> **We found no evidence that the three contraceptive methods differ in vaginal microbiome community composition or in BV prevalence.**

- Community composition: arm explains ~3% of variation, p = 0.15.
- BV prevalence: rates are 49% / 36% / 38%, Fisher p = 0.45.
- In both cases a real signal **is** present in the data — BV status itself
  strongly structures composition (R² = 0.24, p = 0.001) — but that signal is
  evenly distributed across the three arms.

# What we do not believe about our own result

## 

- **We do not believe the arms are identical.** A study of 93 people can only
  rule out fairly large differences; a modest true difference would be
  invisible here.
- **We do not believe we have proven "contraception does not affect the
  microbiome."** We have only shown that this study does not detect an effect
  on whole-community composition or BV prevalence.
- **We do not believe the community-level test tells the whole story.** A
  single species or gene could differ by arm even though the whole community
  does not. That question needs a per-feature test such as DESeq2.

# Thank you

## 

**Next question:** Which individual species or genes differ by arm?
